investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state, meaning the eval runner could not reach any stage of agent lifecycle validation.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules and are ineligible even for preemption. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never produced a running VM, and the eval runner returned zero evidence against the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 256). This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the production-api Kubernetes cluster; it is an eval-detected infrastructure condition, not a confirmed user-traffic outage.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all 6 available nodes, with preemption also exhausted.

failed-check.timing: eval ran for 132018 ms (latencyMs) and ended at 2026-07-08T00:57:35.811Z with status=fail, well within the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000 ms, confirming the pod was stuck unscheduled for 127s before the check gave up.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe never advancing past pod scheduling.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm', '4 node(s) didn't match') with latencyMs=150944, confirming the capacity condition persisted across multiple sequential probe attempts.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler error with latencyMs=151813, further confirming the condition was sustained over the full eval window ending at 2026-07-08T01:02:38.569Z.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; a scheduling failure at this call would prevent any downstream evidence from being written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).
[Likely contributing] The pod's node affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to a subset of nodes (2 out of 6), amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall on those nodes.

[Possible] A quota or limit range on the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource at the namespace or cluster level is set too low relative to concurrent demand, preventing new allocations even if physical capacity exists.

[Possible] Existing remote agent VMs or pods are not being cleaned up promptly, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), but prior failed or leaked runs may not have released resources.

[Lower confidence] The node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods may be overly restrictive, excluding nodes that could otherwise serve the kata.peerpods.io/vm workload if the selector were broadened.

Review the withCleanup logic in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to ensure that eval probe cleanup reliably releases kata.peerpods.io/vm resources even when the pod never reaches a running state (i.e., cleanup of pending/unschedulable pods).

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available and unallocated on the 2 affinity-matching nodes, the scheduling failure would not be a capacity exhaustion issue and another cause (e.g., a misconfigured resource request on the pod spec) would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeded and produced all 4 required evidence keys, the failure would be transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the scheduler message changed on re-run to a different error (e.g., image pull failure, quota exceeded at namespace level, or a different resource), the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis would need to be revised.
If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passed, the failure would be localized to the create path rather than a cluster-wide capacity condition.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined on any node in the cluster, the root cause would be a missing node label or device plugin registration rather than capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-node-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all eligible nodes and fails fast if capacity is at or near zero, before any pod creation is attempted.

Add a remote-agent-cleanup-verify eval that confirms no orphaned remote agent pods remain in a pending or running state after the eval window closes, catching resource leaks before they exhaust cluster capacity.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 nodes with non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity), alerting on topology risk before a full exhaustion event.
Extend the remote-agent-create contract to capture a schedulingLatencyMs evidence key so that slow-but-successful scheduling can be distinguished from unschedulable failures in future eval history.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place any new remote-agent pod because the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were collected and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to run remote-agent pods. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to schedule a new remote-agent pod times out as Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval; whether real provisioning requests are also failing requires separate confirmation.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: the remote-agent-state contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] for the sibling create check, and orgId/agentId/readyState/state for the state check — none of these can be satisfied without a running pod.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes — all concurrent or recently created remote-agent VMs have consumed the full advertised capacity, leaving no slots for new pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist.

[Possible] Node pool scaling is lagging or disabled — the 2 kata-capable nodes have not scaled out to absorb demand, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by node affinity/selector rules that restrict remote-agent pods to kata-capable nodes only.

[Possible] A prior eval run or real workload left orphaned remote-agent VMs running, consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that were not released before this eval run started. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) is designed to release resources, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup it could leave slots occupied.

[Lower confidence] The node affinity or selector on the remote-agent pod spec may have been tightened in a recent deployment, reducing the eligible node pool from more than 2 nodes to exactly 2, making exhaustion more likely. No suspect change in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges supports this directly; it remains a hypothesis requiring pod-spec inspection.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted (i.e., allocatable > used on the eligible nodes), the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are shown to have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the pod affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude them, the root cause shifts to a misconfigured node selector rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and schedules a pod without any capacity change, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent requests that have since completed) rather than a sustained exhaustion.

If the eval runner logs show the probe was skipped due to a missing token (run-status-probes.mjs line 1902 guard) rather than a scheduling timeout, the Unschedulable message would have come from a different code path and the diagnosis would need revision.

If no orphaned remote-agent pods are found running and node capacity is confirmed full, the cause may be a node pool autoscaler failure or a quota limit imposed at the cloud-provider level rather than in-cluster resource exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all eligible nodes and fails with a warning before full exhaustion (e.g., at 80% utilization), providing earlier signal than waiting for a pod to become Unschedulable.
Add an eval that counts running remote-agent pods and compares against the known kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity ceiling, alerting when the headroom drops below a safe threshold.
Add a cleanup-verification eval that checks for remote-agent pods older than the expected maximum lifetime, catching orphaned VMs that the withCleanup wrapper failed to release.
Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and record the pod scheduling latency as evidence, enabling trend detection of degrading scheduling times before full exhaustion occurs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state, meaning the eval runner could not reach any stage of agent lifecycle validation.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules and are ineligible even for preemption. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never produced a running VM, and the eval runner returned zero evidence against the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 256). This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the production-api Kubernetes cluster; it is an eval-detected infrastructure condition, not a confirmed user-traffic outage.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all 6 available nodes, with preemption also exhausted.

failed-check.timing: eval ran for 132018 ms (latencyMs) and ended at 2026-07-08T00:57:35.811Z with status=fail, well within the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000 ms, confirming the pod was stuck unscheduled for 127s before the check gave up.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe never advancing past pod scheduling.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm', '4 node(s) didn't match') with latencyMs=150944, confirming the capacity condition persisted across multiple sequential probe attempts.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler error with latencyMs=151813, further confirming the condition was sustained over the full eval window ending at 2026-07-08T01:02:38.569Z.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; a scheduling failure at this call would prevent any downstream evidence from being written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).
[Likely contributing] The pod's node affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to a subset of nodes (2 out of 6), amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall on those nodes.

[Possible] A quota or limit range on the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource at the namespace or cluster level is set too low relative to concurrent demand, preventing new allocations even if physical capacity exists.

[Possible] Existing remote agent VMs or pods are not being cleaned up promptly, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), but prior failed or leaked runs may not have released resources.

[Lower confidence] The node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods may be overly restrictive, excluding nodes that could otherwise serve the kata.peerpods.io/vm workload if the selector were broadened.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place any new remote-agent pod because the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were collected and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to run remote-agent pods. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to schedule a new remote-agent pod times out as Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval; whether real provisioning requests are also failing requires separate confirmation.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring an orgId; a scheduling failure at this call explains why no evidence is ever written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: the remote-agent-state contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] for the sibling create check, and orgId/agentId/readyState/state for the state check — none of these can be satisfied without a running pod.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes — all concurrent or recently created remote-agent VMs have consumed the full advertised capacity, leaving no slots for new pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist.

[Possible] Node pool scaling is lagging or disabled — the 2 kata-capable nodes have not scaled out to absorb demand, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by node affinity/selector rules that restrict remote-agent pods to kata-capable nodes only.

[Possible] A prior eval run or real workload left orphaned remote-agent VMs running, consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that were not released before this eval run started. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) is designed to release resources, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup it could leave slots occupied.

[Lower confidence] The node affinity or selector on the remote-agent pod spec may have been tightened in a recent deployment, reducing the eligible node pool from more than 2 nodes to exactly 2, making exhaustion more likely. No suspect change in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges supports this directly; it remains a hypothesis requiring pod-spec inspection.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and schedules a pod without any capacity change, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent requests that have since completed) rather than a sustained exhaustion.

If the eval runner logs show the probe was skipped due to a missing token (run-status-probes.mjs line 1902 guard) rather than a scheduling timeout, the Unschedulable message would have come from a different code path and the diagnosis would need revision.

If no orphaned remote-agent pods are found running and node capacity is confirmed full, the cause may be a node pool autoscaler failure or a quota limit imposed at the cloud-provider level rather than in-cluster resource exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all eligible nodes and fails with a warning before full exhaustion (e.g., at 80% utilization), providing earlier signal than waiting for a pod to become Unschedulable.
Add an eval that counts running remote-agent pods and compares against the known kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity ceiling, alerting when the headroom drops below a safe threshold.
Add a cleanup-verification eval that checks for remote-agent pods older than the expected maximum lifetime, catching orphaned VMs that the withCleanup wrapper failed to release.
Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and record the pod scheduling latency as evidence, enabling trend detection of degrading scheduling times before full exhaustion occurs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-08 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster had only 2 nodes eligible for kata peer-pod VMs, both of which reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or receiving a runtime response, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were produced and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod times out as Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent() (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) which requires a scheduled pod; because the pod never starts, no evidence is collected and the contract validation fails with all 5 required fields missing.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: concurrent or lingering remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or real workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new scheduling attempts. Supported by all three sibling checks reporting the same error within a ~5-minute window.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch reducing the eligible node pool to only 2 nodes: if the affinity rules are overly restrictive or if nodes were cordoned, drained, or relabeled, the effective scheduling domain shrinks and exhaustion occurs faster. The message explicitly states 4 of 6 nodes did not match the pod's affinity/selector.

TERTIARY — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from a previous eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them: if withCleanup() in run-status-probes.mjs failed to delete a prior pod, its VM slot would remain consumed. This is consistent with all three checks failing in sequence rather than simultaneously.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — a quota or LimitRange applied to the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource at the namespace or cluster level that was recently tightened, reducing the total allocatable count on the 2 eligible nodes. No quota evidence is present in the packet; this remains speculative.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the production-api cluster immediately: run kubectl describe nodes and check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to quantify the capacity gap.

Identify and clean up any leaked or zombie remote-agent pods that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without active workloads. Verify the withCleanup() wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is executing pod deletion on both success and failure paths.

Determine whether the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector can be made eligible (e.g., by adding the required node labels or relaxing the affinity rules) to increase the scheduling domain beyond 2 nodes.

If VM slot exhaustion is confirmed as sustained, evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes needs to be increased (e.g., by scaling node resources or adding more eligible nodes to the cluster).

Add a pre-flight check to the remote-agent eval runner that queries available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting pod creation, and surfaces a WARN or SKIP status with a descriptive message when capacity is zero, rather than waiting for a scheduling timeout.
Monitor whether the remote-agents checks self-recover on the next scheduled eval run without manual intervention, to distinguish transient from sustained exhaustion.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed ample remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 affinity-matching nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling error message would be inconsistent with actual cluster state and another cause (e.g., a misconfigured resource request in the pod spec) would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks all passed on a subsequent run without any infrastructure change, it would suggest the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a prior eval pod was still terminating) rather than a sustained capacity shortage.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the root cause would be localized to the runtime check's pod spec or configuration rather than a shared cluster capacity problem.

If node affinity rules were found to be intentionally restricting scheduling to 0 eligible nodes (e.g., all matching nodes were cordoned), the cause would be node availability rather than VM slot exhaustion.

If a passing run produced all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) with a message containing 'hello from aura', it would confirm the eval infrastructure is functional and the prior failure was transient.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-node-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on affinity-eligible nodes and fails/warns when capacity drops to zero, providing early warning before pod scheduling attempts time out.

Add a stale-pod detection eval that lists remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 10 minutes) that are still Running or Pending, to catch cleanup failures from withCleanup() before they exhaust VM slot capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3 nodes), alerting when the eligible pool shrinks due to cordoning, draining, or label changes.

Refine the remote-agent-runtime eval to emit a structured SKIP or INFRA_FAIL status with the scheduler error message as evidence when pod scheduling fails, so the contract validation gap (all 5 evidence fields missing) is distinguishable from an application-level response failure.
